title: Tu ou tout ?
en: Pronunciation: the sounds u /y/ and ou /u/
intro: French **u** (/y/) doesn't exist in English, and it's easy to confuse with **ou** (/u/). Many words differ only by this sound: *tu / tout, dessus / dessous, rue / roue*. Train your ear first, then your mouth.

cases.label: u /y/: tu, rue, sur
cases.rule: **u, û** = /y/: say *ee* (/i/), keep your tongue there, and round your lips like for *oo*. *tu, rue, sur, une, salut*.

cases.label: ou /u/: tout, vous, sous
cases.rule: **ou, où, oû** = /u/, like English *oo* in *food*: *tout, vous, sous, jour, rouge*.

cases.label: u or ou: different words
cases.rule: One sound changes the word: *tu / tout, dessus / dessous, rue / roue, vu / vous, sur / sous, pur / pour*.

cases.label: ui /ɥi/: huit, nuit
cases.rule: **ui** = a very quick /y/ gliding into /i/: *huit, nuit, lui, cuisine, depuis*.

cases.label: oui /wi/ vs huit /ɥit/
cases.rule: **oui** starts with /w/ (from **ou**), **huit** with /ɥ/ (from **u**): *oui / huit, Louis / lui*.

cases.label: qu, gu: silent u
cases.rule: After **q**, the **u** is silent: *qui, que, quatre* (/k/). **gu** before e / i = /ɡ/: *guitare*.

sections.title: 1. The sound u /y/
text: Say **ee** (/i/). Keep your tongue exactly there, and push your lips forward into a small round “o”. That's **u**.

examples.en: The book is on the table.
The cat is under the table.
Is the cat on top or underneath?

sections.title: 4. ui /ɥi/
text: **ui** is one quick syllable: start with **u** and slide straight into **i**.

sections.title: 5. oui or huit?
text: **oui** starts like **ou** (lips very round, /w/); **huit** starts like **u** (/ɥ/).

sections.title: 6. qu and gu: a silent u
text: After **q**, the **u** is (almost always) silent: **qu** = /k/. And **gu** before **e** or **i** = a hard /ɡ/.

mistakes.why: That would be **tout**. For **u**, say *ee* with round lips.

story.title: Lou et le loup
story.en: A little fable full of u and ou. Listen first, then read it aloud.

lines.fr: Un jour, Lou se promène dans la {rue|uo-u}.
lines.en: One day, Lou is walking in the street.

lines.fr: Tout à coup, {sous|uo-ou} un arbre, il y a… un {loup|uo-ou} !
lines.en: Suddenly, under a tree, there's… a wolf!

lines.fr: « Bonjour, loup ! {Tu|uo-pairs} es {tout|uo-pairs} seul ? » dit Lou.
lines.en: “Hello, wolf! Are you all alone?” says Lou.

lines.fr: « {Oui|uo-oui}, je suis tout seul. Et toi, tu as peur de moi ? »
lines.en: “Yes, I'm all alone. And you — are you afraid of me?”

lines.fr: « Non ! Je n'ai pas peur. Tu as l'air {doux|uo-ou}. »
lines.en: “No! I'm not afraid. You look gentle.”

lines.fr: Le loup demande : « {Où|uo-ou} vas-tu, petite Lou ? »
lines.en: The wolf asks: “Where are you going, little Lou?”

lines.fr: « Je vais chez ma grand-mère. Elle fait une {soupe|uo-ou} aux légumes. »
lines.en: “I'm going to my grandmother's. She's making vegetable soup.”

lines.fr: « Une soupe ? {Super|uo-u} ! Moi, j'adore la soupe ! »
Alors, Lou et le loup marchent sur la {route|uo-ou}, {sous|uo-pairs} la {lune|uo-u}, pas {sur|uo-pairs} la lune !
lines.en: So Lou and the wolf walk along the road, under the moon — not on the moon!

lines.fr: La grand-mère voit le loup… et elle a très peur !
lines.en: The grandmother sees the wolf… and she's very scared!

lines.fr: Mais le loup est gentil : il mange sa soupe, il dit « merci », et il part dans la {nuit|uo-ui}.
lines.en: But the wolf is kind: he eats his soup, says “thank you”, and leaves into the night.

quiz.q: Which word has the sound /y/, as in « tu »?
Which spelling makes the sound /u/, as in « vous »?
Listen: which word do you hear?

options: /ɥi/ — a quick u gliding into i
quiz.answer: /ɥi/ — a quick u gliding into i

Do « Louis » and « lui » sound the same?
